W5 (contrarian), after E013.
1. Accuracy comes from the optimizer and from averaging. Lookahead added about +1.0 pp (E005), and Muon about +0.66 pp (E006). Muon renormalizes each filter to norm sqrt(out) every step and has no WD term. So the WD knob reaches only BN biases, the whitening bias and the head, and I019 is close to a reshuffle. Decaying LR to 0 cost -0.26 pp (E009), which fits Lookahead already doing the late-phase noise reduction.
2. Lookahead acts on the trajectory, not just the endpoint. Pulling the fast weights back every 5 steps damps Muon's large fixed-norm steps. Near the end the alpha ramp gives a horizon of only about 20 steps, so endpoint averaging alone has little to work with. Prediction: a plain EMA (I022) loses 0.3-0.8 pp. Averaging BN running stats from weights that never reset is a further mismatch.
3. Time is GPU compute, scaling with pixels × width. Gentle resizing saved 20% but cost about 0.6 pp against the Muon base (E006→E007), so it was not free. Going to 20 px fell off a cliff (E011, -1.4 pp). Cutting the last group from 576 to 512 saved 9.4% for -0.43 pp (E010).
4. A step is about 28 ms. With HYP epochs=9.5 at batch 2000, a run is about 237 steps. The host does not sync per step. The only syncs are the 25 boolean-mask copies per epoch in augment, plus the per-epoch interpolate/permute of the full 50k images. So CUDA graphs or graph-break removal can buy about 1.5-4% at most. A mechanism nobody has costed: the per-epoch full-dataset work (augment, antialias interpolate at one or two resolutions, gather into channels_last) runs about 10 times. It could be 3-6% of the run, and could be cut by augmenting only the slices actually used, or by fusing crop and resize into one gather.
5. Noise: compiled runs are deterministic per seed (E012 matched bit-for-bit, time within 0.1%). Time noise is about ±1-2%. Any change to trajectory, RNG use or autotuned kernels reshuffles the 3-seed mean by up to ±0.3 pp. LS 0.3→0.2 moved it by +0.04 pp (E013), i.e. LS is not a lever. The margin is 0.18 pp, so feasibility verdicts are mostly a coin flip on reshuffle.
6. A lever nobody has proposed: accuracy is set in the last 32 px phase, and the max-pool head is sensitive to scale. Moving the 28→32 switch earlier (at about 0.6), or using 24→32 with no 28 phase, may buy accuracy for less time than adding epochs does.
Unsure about: the held-out seed mean from E012 (not reported); the cost of prepare (unpinned 150 MB H2D copy, eigh, reflect pad), which I guess at 0.15-0.3 s; whether max-autotune with cudagraphs coexists with in-place Muon param mutation and the Lookahead foreach copies.

forecasts.reason: The step is GPU-bound at about 28 ms with no per-step syncs, so graphs save about 2%, under 3%. Autotuned kernels reshuffle accuracy.
Muon's fixed-norm filters ignore WD, so only the head and biases change. The result is a reshuffle, not a gain of 0.3 pp or more.
There are few breaks or syncs (only the augment mask indexing), so expect about 1-2% saved, below 3%. Accuracy may stay bit-identical only if RNG use is unchanged.
Lookahead's resets damp Muon's fixed-norm steps. A plain EMA with a horizon of about 20 steps plus averaged BN buffers loses about 0.5 pp.

cruxes: What share of train time goes to the per-epoch full-dataset work (augment mask copies, antialias interpolate, permute/gather) and to prepare (unpinned H2D copy, eigh, pad)? If it is 5% or more, fusing or slicing it beats CUDA graphs.
Is E012's held-out 10-seed mean at or above about 0.753? If seeds 0-2 are lucky, the current tip is fragile, and the next move must buy accuracy, e.g. an earlier 32 px switch, not time.
Does moving the 28→32 switch earlier (or dropping the 28 px phase) raise accuracy per second more than adding epochs? This tests whether the late full-resolution phase sets accuracy.
